В неодносложных словах этого диалекта ударение не падает на гласные исконно верхнего подъема 1-го слога (i < *i, u < *u, ө < *i̮) — в этом случае акцент находится на каком-нибудь гласном непервого слога. new_statements.quote: Идеальным примером, где место ударения зависит от фонетического фактора, является коми-язьвинский диалект. В неодносложных словах этого диалекта ударение не падает на гласные исконно верхнего подъема 1-го слога (i < *i, u < *u, ө < *i̮) — в этом случае акцент находится на каком-нибудь гласном непервого слога. Если же в первом слоге стоят гласные исконно среднего или нижнего подъема (e, o, ȯ, a, u < *o̭, ü < *ȯ̭), то ударение падает на них. Таким образом ударение падает на более звучные гласные, т. е. место ударения в слове зависит от качества (сонорности) гласных ... На слабосонорный гласный 1-го слога вообще ударение не падает: muni·s '(он) ушел', munө· 'идет' и т. д.
new_statements.translation: The ideal example of stress placement depending on a phonetic factor is the Komi-Yazva dialect. In polysyllabic words of this dialect stress does not fall on first-syllable vowels that are etymologically high (i < *i, u < *u, ө < *i̮) — in that case the accent is on some vowel of a non-first syllable. If, however, the first syllable contains vowels that are etymologically mid or low (e, o, ȯ, a, u < *o̭, ü < *ȯ̭), the stress falls on them. Thus stress falls on the more sonorous vowels, i.e. the place of stress in the word depends on the quality (sonority) of the vowels present in the word ... On a weakly sonorous first-syllable vowel stress never falls at all: muni·s 'he left', munө· 'goes', etc.
new_statements.citation: Лыткин, В. И. 1970. Проблема лексического ударения в финно-угорских языках. Acta Linguistica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 20 (3-4): 245-263.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Quality (sonority)-sensitive, unbounded: primary stress goes to the leftmost 'heavy' vowel, where heavy = non-high vowels a, o, ȯ, e plus those surface high u, ü, i that continue Proto-Komi closed mid *o̭, *ȯ̭, *ḙ (i.e. correspond to o, e̮/ö, e in other Komi dialects); light = u, i from *u, *i and ө (< *i̮, phonetically mid today but patterning as high). In practice stress is on the first syllable whenever its vowel is heavy; a light first-syllable vowel is never stressed and stress moves right to a later (heavy) syllable; if the word has only light vowels it is end-stressed (default-to-final stated explicitly by Itkonen 1955: 29 'Gibt es nur leichte Vokale im Worte, so ist das Wort endbetont', cf. Lytkin's munө· 'идет', Itkonen's buzginө·; Lytkin 1961: 33-34 via Normanskaja 2018: 175 adds that first-syllable ө always passes stress to the following syllable). Lytkin stresses there is no initial-stress tendency at all. Monosyllables trivially stressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described by Lytkin 1970 or Itkonen 1955 for Komi-Yazva (StressTyp2 codes secondary stress absent).
new_statements.exceptions: Lytkin 1970: 254-255 'единичные случаи морфологизации': (a) stress on the syllable preceding comparative -žik regardless of its vowel (pö·riś 'old' ~ pö·riśžik); (b) some suffixes attract stress against the quality principle: ordinal -öt (kvi·miś ~ kvimö·t 'third'), diminutive -ik, emphatic -ik/-i; (c) when stress leaves a light-vowel root, preference order among suffixes: plural > case > possessive; (d) certain derivational suffixes (-ölt, causative -öt, adjectival -öl, verbal -ör) keep the stress once it reaches them rather than passing it on to later heavy vowels — but only when syll 1 has a light vowel, so this is 'partial morphologisation within the quality-vocalic system'. Normanskaja 2018: 175 (after Lytkin 1961) hedges 'в большинстве случаев'; Itkonen 'gewöhnlich'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation/inflected word forms ('в неодносложных словах', 'место ударения в слове'); examples include case-inflected forms (mu ~ muśa·ń, va ~ vaśa·ń) so the domain is the phonological word including suffixes. Weight criterion is vowel quality (height/sonority), partly etymological/lexical for surface u, ü, i; no role for vowel length or codas.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Komi-Yazva (Jaz'va, коми-язьвинский, Itkonen's 'Ostpermjakisch') variety of the upper Yazva river, Krasnovishersk district, Perm krai = Glottolog komi1277. Lytkin 1970 and Osnovy 1976 call it 'коми-язьвинский диалект / наречие'. NOTE: the existing catalog unit keyed komi1268 (Komi-Zyrian;, source Itkonen 1955) in fact codes this same lect (its own record says 'komi1277 (lect described)'); the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Yazva', WALS yzv and legacy ST the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Komi' are all this variety. Komi-Zyrian proper (komi1268) has a weight-blind initial tendency and Komi-Permyak proper (komi1269) stem-based ('осново-разноместное') stress, per the same sources. The closely similar quality-driven system of the On'kovo subdialect of Komi-Permyak (Lytkin 1970: 250, 257; Osnovy 1976 §19) is a different lect (komi1269).

new_statements.relation_note: No prose statement, so no quotable rule; the stress marks on 2015 field recordings match the Лыткин 1970 rule that the catalog's existing statement records (non-high first-syllable vowels attract stress, ө repels it, u/i/ʉ split). The 'associated papers by Норманская & Идрисов in Урало-алтайские исследования' named in the citation do not exist as co-authored papers: the journal's tables of contents nos. 16-61 (2015-2026) list no paper by Идрисов and none with a Komi-Yazva title; the associated paper is Норманская 2018 (index 1), which cites Idrisov's field dictionaries.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The dictionary is a database, not a description: it states no rule, but 747 of 1115 phonemic transcriptions carry an acute on the stressed vowel (and 548 of 658 paradigm forms). Tabulated over polysyllables with a marked stress (745): initial 433, medial 91, final 221. First-syllable a, e, o, ø take the stress in 306 of 318 words; first-syllable ʌ (Lytkin's ө) in only 3 of 123, the stress moving right (lʌsnʌ́, lʌʃkʌ́t); first-syllable u (51/150), i (32/91) and ʉ (41/62) split both ways, as Lytkin's etymological rule for the high vowels predicts. So the marked data reproduce the vowel-quality-conditioned placement already in the catalog.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not marked; the transcriptions carry a single acute per word.
new_statements.exceptions: No statement; the data show 3 words with a stressed first-syllable ʌ (n'ʌ́nka, n'ʌ́rnʌ, lʌ́ɕit) and 12 words with a/e/o/ø in the first syllable stressed later (e.g. sartás, ʃabúr, zeród, mødík), some of them Russian loans (kʌsók 'мясо' is flagged 'русс. заим.').
new_statements.identity_note: The dictionary is a 2015 expedition record from Красновишерский район, Пермский край (LingvoDoc metadata; coordinates 60.73 N 58.91 E), i.e. the Yazva-basin core area; Normanskaya 2018 treats Komi-Yazva as a language distinct from Komi-Permyak (as her 2021 paper argues) and contrasts it with the Onkovo subdialect of Komi-Permyak, which she calls more archaic in the same quality-driven system.

new_statements.quote: В современном коми-язьвинском языке действует правило, описанное В. И. Лыткиным, согласно которому постановка ударения в большинстве случаев определяется звуковым составом слова: если в первом слоге многосложных слов находятся неузкие гласные a, o, ȯ, e, они всегда принимают на себя ударение, а гласный ɵ, который в коми-язьвинском принадлежит к среднему подъему, но в других диалектах ему обычно соответствует узкий i̮ всегда вызывает перенос ударения на последующий слог, если такой в слове присутствует. Как ударными, так и безударными в многосложных словах могут быть только коми-язьвинские узкие гласные u, u̇, i [Лыткин 1961: 33—34]. Они притягивают ударение, если в других коми диалектах им соответствуют неузкие o, e̮, e, и отталкивают его, если в других коми диалектах им соответствуют узкие u, i.
new_statements.translation: In modern Komi-Yazva the rule described by V. I. Lytkin operates, by which the placement of stress is in most cases determined by the sound make-up of the word: if the first syllable of a polysyllabic word contains a non-high vowel a, o, ȯ, e, it always takes the stress, while the vowel ɵ, which in Komi-Yazva belongs to the mid series but in other dialects usually corresponds to high i̮, always causes the stress to shift to the following syllable if the word has one. Only the Komi-Yazva high vowels u, u̇, i can be either stressed or unstressed in polysyllabic words [Lytkin 1961: 33-34]. They attract the stress when other Komi dialects have non-high o, e̮, e in their place, and repel it when other Komi dialects have high u, i.
new_statements.citation: Норманская, Ю. В. 2018. Прапермское ударение: внутренняя и внешняя реконструкция. Урало-алтайские исследования 2018, № 3 (30): 33-61. [the 'associated paper' of the listed work; not itself in 'works']

Урало-алтайские исследования. 2018. № 3 (30)' = pdf p. 5 of 30 (only the dot of u̇ is dropped by text extraction: 'u, u, i'). The preceding paragraph on the same page lists '1 словарь коми-язьвинского языка' among the six Komi field dictionaries analysed for stress, as the reader says. Surrounding section (pp. 37-38) adds the diachronic argument (older state: non-high vowels attract, high repel; narrowing produced the modern 'качественно-вокальная акцентуация'; Понарядов 2014: 757 on the Onkovo subdialect being more archaic) and…
new_statements.relation_note: Restates the same Лыткин 1961: 33-34 rule the catalog's existing statement (Лыткин 1970: 250) carries, in the same terms; p. 36-37 confirm that a Komi-Yazva field dictionary (index 0) was collected and analysed for stress and that the rule 'operates' in the modern language. Adds no new placement, only the diachronic interpretation.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress placement is conditioned by first-syllable vowel quality: non-high a, o, ȯ, e always stressed; ɵ never stressed (stress on the next syllable); high u, u̇, i stressed or not depending on their historical source (stressed if from non-high proto-vowels, unstressed if from high ones). Normanskaya adds that this is a secondary, quality-driven reshaping of an older free proto-Permic accent (agreeing with Понарядов 2014 on that point).
new_statements.exceptions: 'в большинстве случаев' (in most cases); the high vowels u, u̇, i are the two-way class; a 'more archaic' state without the vowel-narrowing is attributed to the Onkovo subdialect of Komi-Permyak (Лыткин 1955: 26-27; Баталова 1990: 30-33), quoted from Понарядов 2014: 757.
new_statements.identity_note: The dictionary is a 2015 expedition record from Красновишерский район, Пермский край (LingvoDoc metadata; coordinates 60.73 N 58.91 E), i.e. the Yazva-basin core area; Normanskaya 2018 treats Komi-Yazva as a language distinct from Komi-Permyak (as her 2021 paper argues) and contrasts it with the Onkovo subdialect of Komi-Permyak, which she calls more archaic in the same quality-driven system.

sources.note: pp. 28-29 (txt ll. 389-431 re-read): in 'Ostpermjakisch' (= Komi-Yazva) the accent is mobile and depends on vowel aperture; reflexes of Proto-Permic u, i̮, i are «leicht», all others «schwer»; 'Der Akzent ist gewöhnlich in der Silbe zu finden, die den ersten «schweren» Vokal hat. Gibt es nur «leichte» Vokale im Worte, so ist das Wort endbetont' (po·tkөtnө, go·rtiśań ~ juka·śnө ~ buzginө·, pөčkiśa·ń); mostly initial, shifting only when syll 1 has a high vowel. Supplies the explicit default-to-final clause; this is the source StressTyp2/WALS cite.
